description: WAVE A part 1 of 3 — the server-side DOCX renderer on Render + the golden baseline (the foundation for BOTH the auto-generate and bulk paths). Today the browser fills the .docx (mgmt/frontend/src/docxFill.js, byte-identical to mgmt/frontend-svelte/src/lib/docxFill.ts) and hands filled base64 to the Worker. This feature ports that renderer to mgmt/server-render so Render can FILL (not just convert) a .docx, and proves byte-for-byte parity against a golden baseline captured on main first. Cross-service constraints baked in: (1) the xmldom lockfile trap — docxtemplater pulls deprecated xmldom via docxtemplater-image-module-free, and server-render has NO lockfile + npm install, so the vulnerable xmldom would install; solve it (decision below). (2) getLastRenderReport() is a MODULE-LEVEL SINGLETON — on Render at jobsMaxConcurrent=3 that is a concurrency bug, so the missing-tags/missing-images report MUST travel WITH each fill result, not via shared module state. (3) exact renderer parity: delimiters {start:'{',end:'}'}, nullGetter that blanks-and-records unresolved tags, ImageModule getImage with the 1x1 BLANK_PNG_B64 fallback recording missing images, getSize [100,100]. This feature adds the renderer + a NEW job kind's fill primitive but does NOT yet rewire either production path (that is FEAT-003 and FEAT-004).
steps: Prove-first / golden baseline: on main, write a throwaway-then-committed harness that runs the EXISTING mgmt/frontend/src/docxFill.js renderer (Node can import it; it uses pizzip + docxtemplater + docxtemplater-image-module-free, all in mgmt/frontend deps) against a known small template fixture + known data (include: a resolved tag, an UNRESOLVED tag to exercise nullGetter, and an image tag with both a valid data-URL and a missing/invalid one to exercise the blank-PNG fallback). Capture the output .docx bytes AND the render report (missingTags, missingImages) as committed golden fixtures under mgmt/server-render/test/fixtures/. This is the artifact that proves parity.

Decide and implement the xmldom fix for server-render, and justify it in a code comment + the PR body. Recommended: add a COMMITTED package-lock.json for mgmt/server-render generated with the same `overrides` block the frontends use (redirect xmldom -> @xmldom/xmldom), AND switch render.yaml buildCommand + the CI render-service job to `npm ci`. Because npm NEVER records overrides in a lockfile, ALSO add @xmldom/xmldom as a direct dependency at the pinned version so the resolved tree cannot fall back to vulnerable xmldom. Verify with `npm ls xmldom @xmldom/xmldom` and `npm audit` that no 0.1.x xmldom is present. (Alternative to evaluate and reject-with-reason if chosen otherwise: depend only on @xmldom/xmldom + a direct docxtemplater pin without a lockfile — but render.yaml currently has no lockfile by design, so the safest launch move is to introduce one HERE with npm ci, which also fixes audit Render/offload #10.)

Port the renderer to mgmt/server-render (e.g. src/lib/docxRender.js) reproducing docxFill.js EXACTLY: delimiters {start:'{',end:'}'}, paragraphLoop:true, linebreaks:true, the ImageModule (centered:false, getImage with base64FromDataUrl + BLANK_PNG_B64 1x1 fallback recording missing images, getSize ()=>[100,100]), and the nullGetter that pushes part.value to missingTags and returns ''. CRITICAL DIFFERENCE FROM THE BROWSER: do NOT use a module-level lastRenderReport singleton. The fill function must RETURN { filledBase64, report: { missingTags, missingImages } } so each concurrent job carries its own report. Use Buffer for base64 (Node) in place of the browser atob/Uint8Array.

Add unit tests in mgmt/server-render/test/ that run the new renderer against the SAME fixture+data and assert the output bytes and the returned report equal the golden fixtures from step 1 (byte-for-byte parity). Add a concurrency test: fill two different documents interleaved (Promise.all) and assert each returned report is correct for ITS document — this is the test that would fail against a singleton report and proves the concurrency fix.
Do NOT change any production dispatch path in this feature. The renderer is a new library + tests only; FEAT-003/004 consume it.

Mutation-test the parity + concurrency tests (change a delimiter to the default {{ }}, remove the nullGetter recording, swap the report to a shared module variable) and confirm each mutation makes a test fail; record any surviving mutant as equivalent with a reason.
Commit on a feature branch (e.g. wave-a1-render-docx-renderer). Do NOT push.
acceptance_criteria: mgmt/server-render has a docx-fill renderer that reproduces docxFill.js behaviour (delimiters {}, nullGetter blank+record, blank-PNG image fallback, getSize [100,100]).
The renderer returns the render report PER CALL (no module-level singleton); a concurrency test with two interleaved fills proves each report is correct for its own document.
Golden-fixture parity test: the server renderer's output bytes + report equal the bytes + report captured from the browser renderer on main.
`cd mgmt/server-render && npm ci && npm test` passes (lockfile now committed).
`npm ls xmldom` shows no deprecated 0.1.x xmldom (redirected to @xmldom/xmldom); `npm audit` no longer lists the xmldom advisories.
render.yaml buildCommand and the CI render-service job use npm ci against the committed lockfile.
Mutation check recorded: delimiter/nullGetter/singleton mutations each fail a test.
verification: cd mgmt/server-render && npm ci && npm test
cd mgmt/server-render && npm audit --audit-level=high | grep -i xmldom || echo 'no xmldom advisory'
findings:
DONE on branch wave-a1-render-docx-renderer, branched off main (3cc8529), independent of FEAT-001 (wave-c). Commits: eaa9f3c (feature) + 0e38363 (override caret fixup). NOTE: the task-state files (task.json/context.json/FEAT-002.json) live only on the wave-c branch; I brought just those bookkeeping files onto this branch (no FEAT-001 code) so status could be recorded.

BASELINE (prove-first): built a deterministic small .docx fixture (test/fixtures/make-template.mjs -> template.docx, 1299 B) with a resolved tag {name}, an unresolved tag {missing}, a valid-image tag {%photo} (1x1 red PNG data-URL), and an invalid-image tag {%missingPhoto}. capture-golden.mjs ran the LIVE browser renderer mgmt/frontend/src/docxFill.js in Node (Node-22 global atob works) over template+data and committed golden.docx.b64 + golden.report.json. Golden report = {missingTags:['missing'], missingImages:['missingPhoto']}. KEY FINDING about the image fallback: docxtemplater-image-module-free only calls getImage when the tag value is TRUTHY (a falsy/empty value renders empty tag-text and getImage is never reached), so to genuinely exercise the blank-PNG fallback + missingImages recording the missingPhoto value must be a truthy-but-invalid data-URL ('data:image/png;base64,' with empty payload), not '' — documented in data.mjs.

PORT: src/lib/docxRender.js reproduces docxFill.js exactly (delimiters {start:'{',end:'}'}, paragraphLoop:true, linebreaks:true, ImageModule centered:false + getSize ()=>[100,100] + getImage base64FromDataUrl->BLANK_PNG fallback recording missingImages, nullGetter pushes part.value to missingTags and returns ''). Node Buffer replaces atob/Uint8Array. CONCURRENCY FIX: no module-level lastRenderReport singleton; fillDocxTemplateFromBase64/FromBytes RETURN { filledBase64, report }.

PARITY RESULT: every ZIP entry of the ported renderer's output is byte-identical to the golden baseline ([Content_Types].xml, _rels/.rels, word/_rels/document.xml.rels, word/document.xml, word/media/image_generated_1.png, word/media/image_generated_2.png all IDENTICAL) and the returned report equals golden. WHY PER-PART not whole-file bytes: a .docx is a ZIP whose local file headers embed a modification TIMESTAMP that PizZip stamps at generate() time, so two runs of the SAME renderer over the SAME input differ only in those timestamp bytes (verified: same length, first divergence at byte offset 226 inside a local header, all content parts identical). Pinned docxtemplater to EXACT 3.69.3 (frontend's version; server had resolved 3.70.0) so the rendering engine matches production, and a test asserts the pinned version. This is the honest, robust reading of 'byte-for-byte parity of the rendered document'.

CONCURRENCY RESULT: docxRender.test.mjs has (a) an independent-fills test (DATA has a missing image, DATA_B supplies both -> different reports) and (b) a concurrency test interleaving 25 pairs of two DIFFERENT documents via Promise.all, asserting each result carries ITS OWN report. Both pass; both fail against a singleton (see mutants).

XMLDOM DECISION (recommended path taken): added docxtemplater(3.69.3 exact)+pizzip+docxtemplater-image-module-free, the frontends' overrides block (xmldom -> @xmldom/xmldom), @xmldom/xmldom as a DIRECT dep, a COMMITTED package-lock.json, and switched render.yaml buildCommand + the CI render-service job to `npm ci`. DEVIATION from the briefing's suggested EXACT pins: npm rejects an exact-pin override for a package that is also a direct dependency (EOVERRIDE), AND the repo-wide security test mgmt/backend/test/dependency-security-floors.test.mjs only accepts caret-form override ranges (^x.y.z) — so both the override and the direct dep use ^0.9.12 (the same form the frontends use). The committed lockfile still resolves @xmldom/xmldom@0.9.12 EVERYWHERE, which is what actually ships under npm ci. `npm ls xmldom @xmldom/xmldom` shows: '@xmldom/xmldom@0.9.12', 'xmldom@npm:@xmldom/xmldom@0.9.12' (via image-module), 'docxtemplater -> @xmldom/xmldom@0.9.12 deduped' — no 0.1.x anywhere. `npm audit --audit-level=high` reports 0 vulnerabilities and no xmldom advisory. This also fixes audit Render/offload #10 (no lockfile at deploy). The pre-existing dependency-security-floors test now scans the new lockfile and passes.

MUTATION RESULTS (committed eaa9f3c BEFORE mutating; each mutant reverted via git checkout): (1) delimiters {{ }} -> 6/7 tests fail (parity + reports + branch tests). KILLED. (2) remove the nullGetter missingTags recording -> 4/7 fail incl. 'nullGetter records the unresolved tag' + parity + per-call. KILLED. (3) swap the per-call report to a shared module-level variable (the original singleton bug) -> 5/7 fail incl. the per-call test (6) and the concurrency test (7). KILLED. No surviving mutants.

VERIFICATION (all pass): `cd mgmt/server-render && npm ci && npm test` = 188 pass / 0 fail (7 new docxRender tests included); `npm ls xmldom @xmldom/xmldom` no 0.1.x; `npm audit` no xmldom advisory. Also confirmed mgmt/backend suite still green (1045 pass / 0 fail), including the dependency-security-floors and render-batch-contract drift tests. Did NOT touch collectionQueue.js, renderJobs.js, docxTemplates.js, the byte contract, or any frontend production path (FEAT-003/004 scope). node_modules is gitignored; not committed. Did NOT push (per constraints).
